tldr: SELF-RAG is a framework that trains a single arbitrary LM to adaptively retrieve passages on-demand and self-reflect via special reflection tokens, significantly improving generation quality and factuality without sacrificing versatility.
contributions: Proposes Self-Reflective Retrieval-Augmented Generation (SELF-RAG) framework with on-demand retrieval and self-reflection
Introduces reflection tokens (Retrieve, ISREL, ISSUP, ISUSE) unified as next-token predictions from expanded vocabulary
Develops a customizable decoding algorithm enabling inference-time control over retrieval frequency and output quality
Trains critic model offline using GPT-4 generated reflection tokens, eliminating need for critic at inference
methods: SELF-RAG trains two models: a critic C and generator M, both initialized with Llama 2-7B. The critic is trained on 4k-20k supervised examples per token type generated by prompting GPT-4, achieving over 90% agreement with GPT-4 predictions. The generator is trained end-to-end on a curated corpus interleaved with reflection tokens and retrieved passages using standard next-token prediction. At inference, the model uses threshold-based adaptive retrieval and segment-level beam search with critique token probabilities weighted by hyperparameters to customize behavior.
results: SELF-RAG (7B and 13B parameters) significantly outperforms state-of-the-art LLMs and retrieval-augmented models on six tasks including reasoning and long-form generation. Specifically, it outperforms retrieval-augmented ChatGPT on four tasks, and Llama2-chat and Alpaca on all tasks. It shows significant gains in factuality and citation accuracy for long-form generations relative to these models.
limitations: Data collection relies on GPT-4 which raises API costs and reproducibility concerns; the approach processes multiple retrieved passages in parallel which may impact efficiency; the paper does not report detailed runtime or computational cost comparisons against baselines.
